Miguel de Cervantes, Don Quixote, Part I chapters 1–8, John Ormsby translation (1885), public domain, Project Gutenberg 996. Original text consulted 2026-10-13: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/996/996-h/996-h.htm#ch2 . This episode adapts chapters 2–3 only, following the existing chapter-1 sidekick episode. The classroom translation has not been independently verified.

Source event sequence: first departure before dawn; discovery he is not knighted; uneventful hungry day's ride; inn mistaken for castle; women and supper, helmet ribbons and drinking reed; request for knighthood; innkeeper's practical supplies advice; armour on trough; first carrier struck unconscious; second carrier badly hurt; companions throw stones; host and fear end attack; wounded carried away; hurried ceremony using straw/barley account book, candle, neck blow and sword-tap; Tolosa belts sword, Molinera attaches spur; departure without payment demanded. These outcomes do not branch. Opening arrival compresses daytime travel into a recap. Stable conversations use the courtyard backdrop as a continuous theatrical setting.

All dialogue is original modern adaptation, not verbatim quotation. Student helper, choices, warnings, aid, classroom and one-question journal are invented connective material. Student is not Sancho; he first joins in chapter 7. Tolosa is a traveller, not the innkeeper's employee. Non-graphic presentation retains serious injuries. Departing carriers leave the frame because they fall out of view, not because they recover. No random event changes Cervantes's plot.

Visual staging: generic versioned manga cloth costumes, including Quixote's existing brown tunic, stand in for period clothing. Armour, helmet, lance, sword, reed and horse are narrated/mimed rather than rendered props. Bow stands in for kneeling; actor rigs return to standing after a gesture. Molinera, candle-bearing boy and crowd remain offscreen; their source actions are narrated. No generated video or speech.

Weekly vocabulary continuity: World Literature W09 Oct 12–16, David's CORE_VOCAB_BY_WEEK.txt: intertextuality, adaptation, revision, close reading, derivative, judicious. Used where natural; no assumption of a new assigned teaching date.
